_why: Skill updates bring back long upstream descriptions. apply_descriptions.py puts these short ones back when the upstream text is the one recorded in 'upstream' (a fingerprint), and reports the skill when the upstream text is new, so the short version gets rewritten from the latest text. 'upstream': null means not recorded yet; the next update will report it once.

archify.short: Use when visualizing systems, API calls, pipelines, schemas, histories, timings, or everyday steps, parts and states as explorable HTML diagrams (architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, state, ERD, class, tree, timeline, waterfall), from requirements, Mermaid or the repo. Also turns an answer into a one-page explainer when the user asks for a page or explainer (做成一页, 用页面讲) or their rules opt in with an [archify explainer: ...] line. Not for dashboards.

better-accessibility.short: Use when reviewing or fixing accessibility: keyboard and focus behavior, ARIA, accessible names, forms, screen-reader announcements, motion and zoom, against WCAG 2.2.

better-colors.short: Use when building or checking a color system: generating palettes, naming semantic tokens, converting between formats and measuring contrast.

better-interface.short: Use when reviewing a whole screen, flow or interface for problems across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color, UI polish and motion, returned as one ranked report.

better-layout.short: Use when setting or reviewing grouping, alignment, reading order, responsive structure and room for translated text, so a layout holds up when resized, translated or mirrored.

better-typography.short: Use when setting or reviewing how text renders: type scale, spacing, font features, wrapping, truncation and punctuation.

better-ui.short: Use when polishing surfaces and icons with exact values for border radius, optical alignment, shadows and icon states.

better-writing.short: Use when writing or reviewing interface copy (labels, errors, empty states, confirmations) so it matches the product's voice and tells people what to do next.

find-skills.short: Use when the user asks "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or wants to find and install an agent skill for a task.

frontend-design.short: Use when building new UI or reshaping an existing one and it needs a distinctive, intentional visual direction: aesthetic choices, typography, and avoiding templated defaults.

humanizer.short: Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells (not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes everywhere, inflated claims, sales language, stock AI words, bold labels, filler). Rewrites it to read like the writer without changing what it says.

ui-demo.short: Use when the user asks for a demo, walkthrough, screen recording or tutorial video of a web app. Records a WebM with Playwright, a visible cursor and natural pacing.

web-design-guidelines.short: Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices". Reviews UI code against the Web Interface Guidelines.

orchestration.short: Use for /orchestration, Orca workers or supervision (monitor, task DAGs, ask/reply, decision gates), splitting or fanning out code changes across agents, worktrees or branches, or another agent working and reporting back ("Have Codex review this and report back"). Also when you are a dispatched worker (Task and Dispatch IDs: ask, worker_done). Not for plain searches and reads, which stay with your own subagents unless Orca or a named agent is asked for. Hand-offs with nothing expected back go to orca-cli.

orca-cli.short: Use for "$orca-cli", Orca worktrees, child worktrees, spawning codex/claude in a worktree, read/wait/send Orca terminal, handoff/handover, give this to or ask/tell/message another agent (including a paired Orca server), Orca browser, or opening, testing or screenshotting a web page in Orca unless another browser tool is named. Not for plain curl/fetch. Prefer over raw git worktree, ad hoc PTYs or Computer Use when Orca state is involved.

orca-computer-use.short: Use only when a local app window needs GUI control a shell, file, git, HTTP or CLI path cannot do: clicks, typing, menus, dialogs and screenshots in native apps, Chrome, Edge, Safari or webviews, in the background through `orca computer`. Not for Orca's embedded browser (orca-cli).

impeccable.short: Use to design, redesign, critique, audit, polish or animate a frontend: websites, landing pages, dashboards, app UI, components, native iOS/Android screens, or a design system (DESIGN.md).

diagram-design.short: Branded diagrams and charts as HTML/SVG/PNG. Use when the user asks for an architecture (current-state, delta, deployment), flowchart, sequence, swimlane, state machine, ER/schema, UML class, timeline, Gantt, org chart, tree, layer stack, Venn, pyramid/funnel, quadrant, radar, treemap, Sankey, fishbone, Wardley map, kanban, user journey, service blueprint, story map, medallion, data flow, DP integration or DP security matrix diagram, or a bar, line, scatter, heatmap or waterfall chart. Imports .drawio, Mermaid and .excalidraw.

retro.short: Use when the user asks for a retro or retrospective on a coding session.

grill-lite.short: Use when the user says grill me, grill-lite, interview me, ask me your questions first, stress-test this plan, or wants to think a plan, purchase or idea through before acting. Asks numbered rounds of questions, then saves the decisions in a short note.

better-motion.short: Use when deciding what should animate or building it: transitions, enters and exits, icon swaps, shared layout animation and drag, with exact duration, easing, scale and distance.
